**Submitted: deviation (T4C), preferred level.**

Repairs made in this round, in operative language:

1. **Section number now inline in the operative text** — the clause reads "11.3 Termination for Convenience. …", so the numbering renders consistently with §§ 11.1–11.2 and matches the "Section 11.3" citation in the comment and rationale (the earlier `numbering` parameter was not surfacing in the rendered paragraph).
2. **Customer party identified generically as well as by name** — "Corio, as the customer, may terminate this Agreement for convenience …", so the grant is unambiguous on its face that the convenience right runs to the customer.

All four preferred elements remain carried by the single insertion: customer convenience termination of the Agreement; thirty (30) days' prior written notice; pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period; and no Commerce One convenience termination during the initial five-year term or any renewal term.

No other text was touched: § 11.1 (term/auto-renewal), § 11.2 (breach, insolvency, Software-specification material condition) and § 11.3's former neighbours remain verbatim, and no survival tail, expense, procedure, "in whole or in part", or pre-emptive "notwithstanding" language was added. The fallback (60–90 days' notice with a three-month fee cap) is offered only as a negotiating step in the comment. Validation returned `ok:true` with minimality clean.
